title: Revision Studio
concept: A dark registration table turns P&ID change control into a tangible act of aligning translucent engineering sheets. Cool original ink and warm revision ink share the same stable equipment geometry. A local coral revision cloud encloses the added bypass without obscuring the original valve route. The sequence ends in a bound review packet with a deliberately open review seal: generated geometry and linked evidence are proposals, not engineering approval. All diagram data is illustrative, not performed engineering.
metaphor: A drafting studio registering original and revised sheets, then binding a traceable review packet.
choreography: Two rotated translucent sheets slide apart to expose original and proposed revisions of the same equipment.
The sheets converge on registration crosses; equipment ports and connection points become visible without changing identity.
The base state keeps a single valve route. Add bypass draws a second branch around the valve, its two tie-in points and a local redline cloud.
A drawing is indexed into three trace lines: the retained original, linked route or change, and unresolved inputs. Review remains required.
The registered layers assemble into a clipped packet; an incomplete review seal and explicit proposed/not-approved footer preserve the human decision boundary.
interaction: The supplied Base route / Add bypass choice switches the phase-two drawing between the existing pump-and-valve path and an additional parallel branch around the valve. The redline cloud, tie-in nodes, route-count caption and accessible description all change. The selected branch is carried into the review and outcome drawings.
contributions: A pure reusable engineering-sheet primitive with translucent paper, folded corner, drafting grid, sheet numbering and stable equipment geometry.
A registration and local redline motion vocabulary that animates geometry with finite draw, alignment and staged-evidence sequences while leaving the static artwork complete.
A traceable review composition that explicitly distinguishes original evidence, proposed change and unresolved input without implying approved engineering.
limitations: All equipment, connectivity, revision identifiers and route counts are authored illustrative examples. No engineering analysis, imported drawing recognition or approval is performed.
The route count describes the two depicted graphical paths, not a verified hydraulic scenario enumeration.
The host owns language selection and user controls. This module supplies English SVG text plus authored Korean translation pairs.
Validation covers module syntax, deterministic output, SVG structure, translation coverage and identifier isolation. Browser, physical-device and user acceptance remain host-level checks.
